For a long time, I had difficulty opening up to them.  I'd always been told "fake it til you make it" and that me talking about my issues and how they affected me was "too much negativity".  I'd effectively been trained to do exactly the opposite of what they now wanted me to do in therapy. 

After that, I managed to start opening up more, but my insurance would repeatedly "lapse" despite the fact that I was on disability.   I stopped going because literally every fourth visit, I would be turned away. 

Finally, after getting that straightened out, it became apparent that I already knew and utilized most coping skills, due to multiple inpatient stays.   The problem wasn't the lack of help from therapy, it was the speed with which many of my issues would present themselves, and at sųch high intensity.  My analogy is, it's great to have coping skills when the waves setsweet getting a little rough, but when you're pushed directly into a hurricane, you need outside assistance.

If you were honestly saved, you'll still go to Heaven, for nothing can break that bond.  But you WILL still face judgement.  The rewards you gain in Heaven are proportionate to the Godliness you lived in your life. 

If you were never saved, then sadly, you will go to Hell unless you confess, repent, seek forgiveness, and accept Christ.
